lines.text: The clocks on GPS satellites run fast.
Just over thirty-eight millionths of a second, every single day.
But left uncorrected, the timing error alone would equal kilometres of distance, in a single day.
So the clocks on older satellites were set down before launch, to cancel it out.
But why would a clock in orbit run fast at all? And how high up are they? That's level nine, and the full video is linked right here.
